newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges lower as profits taken.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges lower as profits taken.

text.p: White sugar futures edged lower on Wednesday morning as players took profits after the recent bout of fund-led buying which drove benchmark October to a new life-high.
Persisent fund buying through commission houses pushed October up $5.50 to $330.20 late on Tuesday, the culmination of two strong sessions.
"The opinion seems to be that it was slightly overdone although I don't think we're looking at a black hole," said one trader.
"People are a little nervous of going long here -- but the market looks quite good."
On the spreads, traders said there was more interest in dealing the October/March differential, rather than October against December.
December is traditionally less of a liquid forward month, partly as there is no corresponding month on the New York market for arbitrage trading.
At 1130 GMT October was down $1.70 at $328.00 and December down $1.30 at $322.50. Volume was mostly in October and amounted to 558 lots.
The spot contract also dominated activity on the Paris market, which traders said was likely to be pre-hedging in advance of the weekly European Union tender for sugar export licences.
October was $1.00 lower at $327.50 and December down 90 cents at $322.10. Matif volume was 500 lots.
